New hull	 1,500
Decked scow or barge provided with derrick, hoisting engine and ' clamshell ' or ' orange-peel' bucket for dredging boat harbours, &e., in Prince Edward Island, where services of ordinary dredging plant are unavailable, and for transportation of materials required for day labour
works	 3,000
One hydraulic dredge with 15-inch, suction pipe, complete	 70,000

We have decided to put the ' New Dominion. ' on the scrap heap, as she has outlived her usefulness, so that $28,500 of this will not be spent, and should we not get the suction dredge it would take off $65,000, making $205,000, leaving just about what we are asking, $180,000. But we are in this position that, having decided to put the ' New Dominion ' on the scrap heap, we will be left somewhat short of dredging plant in the maritime provinces, and we ought to obtain an additional dredge. However, we are asking $180,000. It may be that we can postpone the obtaining of some of the tugs and put the money into a dredge to take the place of the 'New Dominion.' That we have not decided, and will not without careful consideration with the superintendent of dredging and the other officers of the department who have given special attention to this subject.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: I understand that the government loaned two or more of their scows to the Maritime Dredging and Construction Company.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: They hired them.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: At what rate?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: I think $10 a day for each one.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Are they still under hire?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: I think so.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext:
They have been under hire how long, two or three years?
Mr. iPUGSLEY.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: The Dredging Company had two at Gaspereau in the fall of 1908, and the chief engineer says they have two at St. John. These scows were not in use in connection with the government dredges, and I think they are still under hire at $10 a day.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Were not those the scows from the dredge ' W. S. Fielding'?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: No. I think not; I think they were brought from Nova Scotia. They had been used in connection with another dredge.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Will the new scows be built by contract?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Those built in our shipyard at Ottawa would be built by our own men and most if not all of the others by public tender.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Is it not a new departure for the government to hire out dredges?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: These are not dredges; they are two scows.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: I did not know that they were so plentiful that my hon. friend would go into the business of hiring them out. Where will we find the total revenue from these scows in the past year?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: I can easily get the figures for my hon. friend.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: What will be the total cost of these dredges?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: They are not dredges; they are scows. I shall get the value.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: These are steel scows, and cost about $11,000 each.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: For what were they originally used by the government?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: In connection with a dredge in Nova Scotia, but we had no immediate use for them, and it was considered good business to keep them in use if we could get a good rental for them.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Have they been rented for two years?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: They were rented in the fall of 1908, and used at Gaspereau. They are not large scows. Those used at Gaspereau have a capacity of only 210 cubic yards.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Are the company hiring them doing government work?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Doing government dredging.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: That is a remarkable condition of things.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Why? Would the hon. gentleman suggest it is better to keep the scows idle than to hire them out at a good rental?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: As I understand there is a good deal of work in different parts of this country for scows of that kind. If the government do not require the scows it would be better to sell them than to rent them. I do not believe the people desire the government to go into the construction of scows to be rented to contractors who are contracting for the government.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: The best policy would be to sell them if they were no longer required, provided a good price could be got for them, but pending that sale I think it would be thoroughly good business if, instead of keeping them lying up rusting, not earning any money, they should be hired out at a good, fair rental.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Has my hon. friend made any effort to -sell them?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Not yet.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: That is the point. We say it is not good policy to lease them if they could be sold. My hon. friend's department has had them leased almost two years, and he now says it is better to sell them. I understand that these scows are not very long lived, they do not stand work any considerable length of time, and I am not quite sure whether even $10 a day for a portion of the year will be sufficient to pay the government, but whether or not, I must express my disapproval of the government having a considerable amount of money invested in scows, which they are leasing to contractors that are working for this government. That is a policy the people would not approve of, and I am sure my hon. friend himself would not approve of it. In fact, he has almost said so. If the department has decided thaif these are no longer of service to the government, they should sell them and put the money in the treasury, and not have this bartering with contractors. How many days did they work last year?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: I am sorry I have no memorandum of the number of days, but would be glad to get the information and send a note to my hon. friend later, or lay it on the table.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: I would ask the hon. minister if the Maritime Dredging and Construction Company has not, in -addition to these two scows, the lease or hire of a large number of scows belonging to the ' Fielding,' including a scow that cost originally some $24,000? Is that under hire, and at what rate, and for how long?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: I sh-all get the information. Does my hon. friend want to know about the hiring of any other scow?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: The minister might bring down full information.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: I shall be very glad to do that.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Does the hon. minister not know whether the statement of the hon. member for St. John (Mr. Daniel) is correct or not?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: I do not.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: He ought to know, if he has a large number of scows in his department-, whether he is using them himself or leasing them to some one else.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Neither the deputy nor the chief engineer can tell me at present, but I shall get the information.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: I would like a statement of the number of cubic yards dredged by each of these during the last season, and the places where the work was doe.e, and also the cost.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: A return which the right hon. the Prime Minister brought down the other day contains all that information for the last four years. I do not know that it contains the information of the year expiring, but it does for the four preceding years. I could get the information for the present year, but that would be quite a job. Does my hon. friend not think that if he looked at that return, that would satisfy him?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: I think that would probably do.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: At page 280 of the Auditor General's Report, I find, purchase price of dredge ' Industry ' and plant, G. W. Phillips, $157,378.78; custom duty, 25 per cent on $157,379, $39,344.75. Was that purchased after public competition, or in what way?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: It was purchased after most -careful examination and valuation by the superintendent of dredging. It was a comparatively new dredge which had cost a great deal more money, but owing to conditions, those who owned it had no immediate use for it, and it was purchased on very favourable terms.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: How did they come to pay the duty?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Under the rule, every department has to contribute to the customs.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Was this item passed last year?	.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Yes.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: The dredge ' Industry ' is put down in the returns at $150,000, and the. minister says she costs more.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: There was some plant in addition and a duty of $39,000.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: According to this return, the total cost of the dredge ' Industry ' is $150,000.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Then there were the spare parts which made up the difference. You will see it all in the account.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Did she require a new boiler after you purchased her?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Yes. And I insisted on a reduction of $10,000 in the price.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: But you said it was purchased after very careful inspection.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext:
Yes, and we insisted on a reduction of $10,000 in the price owing to the necessity of putting in & new boiler.
. Mr. BLAIN. Does that $10,000 appear in the purchase price in the Auditor General's Report?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: No.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: What is the explanation of the discrepancy between what appears in the return and the facts? The return shows that the dredge -cost $150,000, and the Auditor General's Report $196,734. The House must surely be misled in trying to reach an understanding of the actual cost.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: The hon. member for St. John (Mr. Daniel) has kindly handed me the return. The amount shown here of $150,000 is a mistake, and the figure in the Auditor General's Report is correct. The price should have been shown as $157,000.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Is the duty part of the cost?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Part of the cost to the Public Works Department, but not to the country. The price of the dredge originally was $150,000, if I remember rightly. We had a special examination by experienced engineers, these gentlemen discovered a latent defect in the boiler. My recollection is that we then insisted that $10,000 should be taken off the price, and this was agreed to. Then we had to pay for the spares, of course, and for the actual cost of removing her from where she was to Cornwall.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: What, then, was the total cost?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: The total cost was $157,378.78, which included the spare parts and also the co3t of bringing the vessel from where she was to Cornwall.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: That does not include the duty?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Then there was the duty of $39,344.75.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: And the new boiler cost $4,650?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: No, $9,300; nearly the amount that we deducted-$10,000- for the defect in the boiler.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: According to that she was purchased for $150,000, and after she was purchased

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext:
No. This is what took place:	The price agreed upon-I do not
mean the binding price, but the price which the superintendent of dredging arrived at as fair-I think I am right in saying was $150,000. We decided to have a full examination made by experts. These experts discovered a latent defect in the boiler. The superintendent of dredging reported that there should be a deduction of $10,000 on this account.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Making $140,000.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Yes. The rest would be made up of the cost of spare parts and the cost of bringing her into Canada.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: What are spare parts?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: An extra dipper and buckets, chains, and every thing of that kind.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Are these not included in the price of a dredge?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: No, they figure the spare parts as separate. They are in duplicate.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: What is her capacity?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: She has a large capacity -carries an eight-yard dipper.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: She is not as large as the ' Cynthia ', or the ' Beaver ', in St. John.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: I think so.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: They have nine-yard dippers.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: The ' Industry ' has the capacity to swing a ten-yard dipper.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: What about the length of arm? How deep can she dredge?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: The chief engineer tells me, 48 feet.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: What about $150 for legal expenses in this connection? Did the hon. minister have a lawsuit over the boiler?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: That was to get the title completed.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Title?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Yes, of course-registration.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Changing from United States register.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: The hon. gentleman (Mr. Blain) will know that the $150 would be taxed by the Justice Department.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: How much duty was paid?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: We paid on $157,390.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: And the dredge cost $140,000.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: But the spares and everything went in on the cost and duty would be paid on the whole.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Was there not a reduction of $10,000 on account of the boiler?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Yes, on the dredge itself. But, in making that reduction the cost of spare parts and every thing brought it up $157,378.78, on which we paid a duty of twenty-live per cent.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: I do not know whether I understood correctly or not, but I think the minister said, that while this duty was chargeable to the Public Works Department the country did not pay it.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Yes.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Was the dredge brought into the country free of duty? It used to be the rule that goods brought into the country for the use of the government came in free of duty. Is that the case stm?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: No, that rule lias been done away with. If any department now imports for its own use goods that would be dutiable if imported by a private individual, the duty is paid to the Customs Department by the branch of government importing the article.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: That i3 what I thought. But I understood the minister to say that while this was chargeable to the Public Works Department, it did not cost the country anything.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Exactly, because it is taking money out of one pocket and putting it into another.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Is it not taken out of the consolidated revenue?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Yes, and it goes into the consolidated revenue.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: How?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: By the Finance Minister. It goes to the Finance Minister, it is drawn from the Finance Minister to pay the Minister of Customs, and the Minister of Customs puts it back into finance again.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: It simply has the effect of making the income of the country appear much greater than it really is.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: And the expenditure of the country as well so much greater. It is as broad as it is long.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext:
I would imagine that if one of us was to purchase that dredge for
$150,000, and he paid 25 per cent duty on it, it would come out of his finances, it must have been paid for; and in case of the country, the country must pay for it.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: But where did the duty go to?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: The duty must go to the Customs Department. But it is paid out all the same. When you come to give a statement to this House as to what that article costs, it seems to me that statement would not be correct unless you included in it the duty paid on that article. So the return brought down cannot be correct, financially speaking, when it only discloses the cost of the dredge without the duty.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: There has evidently been a mistake of the clerk in making up that return, a mistake of $7,000.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: May there not possibly be other mistakes in regard to other dredges mentioned?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: It might be, of course. The returns never come under my notice at all. I do not suppose that, ordinarily, they come under the notice of the deputy as to details. The proper clerks are given directions to make up these returns from the papers on file; and I suppose that the clerk has seen the first report which put the price at $150,000 without the spare parts, and he has taken that without his attention being called to the reduction by reason of this latent defect in the boiler. That, I assume, is the way it has occurred. I will see how it has occurred, and if my hon. friend desires, I will get a memo of the exact cost, and how that item of $157,000 has been made up.	.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: I think it is simply another typographical error.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: No, it would be an error of the clerk in making copies.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Should not the $9,000, the cost of the boiler, be added to it?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: That is not a part of the original cost. I do not know, I am inclined to think my hon. friend is right, I think it should be added.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: I think the return is very wrong.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: No, I think the clerk has not added in the cost of the boiler, because that was obtained afterwards.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Therefore, the return is $16,000 wrong on the price.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: No.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext:
As I understand it, the return moved for-my hon. friend will cor-

rect me if I am in error-showed that this dredge cost $150,000; that is the return. Now, we turn up the Auditor General's Report and we find the first item is $157,000, that is $7,000 wrong. Then another item comes in afterwards of $9,000 for the boiler. These two items add $16,000 to the cost that were not added to the cost when the return was brought down to the House.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: I understand that my hon. friend is not reflecting on me at all, nor on my deputy; but it is a question of the clerk in copying. IF is doubtful to my mind whether the clerk, in copying, should put in the dunlicate equipment. A dredge is a dredge without that duplicate equipment, which is only procured as a matter of precaution. You have to keep that duplicate equipment on hand in case of a breakdown; it is like stores. It would have been erroneous if the clerk had put that in as part of the dredge.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Was it complete without that?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Perfectly complete without it. It is like the dredge 'Fielding.' We are asking now, in this vote for dredging plant, an amount to procure a duplicate chain of buckets for the dredge 'Fielding.' Now, if you ask what the dredge cost, it would not be proper to add that in, because that is a duplicate equipment.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: All the same, the minister will allow that there is never a dredge put to work in any part of the country that has not duplicate parts ready. As he knows well, dredges are always breaking down, something is giving away, the spuds break, or something happens to the dipper, and it is impossible to work an ordinary dredge without duplicating parts of it.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Yes, and in the same way no farmer works a farm without having on it horses and cattle, and ploughs, and harrows, and wagons; and yet if I wanted to buy his farm, and he said the price was $5,000, he would think it absurd for me ta say: Why all your horses, and cattle, and ploughs, and harrows, and wagons have come in, because you could not use your farm without those.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: I think the minister's illustration is not apropos. He might as well include coal for working a dredge as for a farmer to include all the stock on the farm, unless you are buying the stock.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext:
All I can say is this: I would not necessarily blame the clerk, because in putting in the cost, of the dredge he did not include the cost of the duplicate parts. Neither will I blame him because he did not add in the customs duty, Mr. BLAIN.
or the cost of a boiler which was put in after the dredge was purchased. But my hon. friend can see there is nothing concealed, because here, on page B-280 of the-report, is given the total cost of the boiler which was purchased afterw'ards, and the cost of duplicating the spare parts.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: But the minister stated that the return brought down was correct. If it is not correct, how much should be added in order to make it a complete statement?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: My view is that, strictly speaking, it is correct, that it gives the cost of the dredge correctly; but it does not include the cost of the boiler, which was obtained afterwards.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: The boiler alone was $9,000.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: $9,300. That does not include the duty which wrent out of one pocket, and was paid into the other. It was paid by the Public Works Department into the Department of Customs. It is a matter of argument whether it ought to have been included or not.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: And that does not include the $7,000 paid for parts?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: No, it does not include the duplicate parts.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Does my hon. friend say that when a return is asked for, and ordered by the House as to the cost of this dredge it is a correct return when it does not include the boilers, and parts of this dredge? Does my hon. friend suggest that .the dredge would work without these parts costing $7,000?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Yes.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Would it be complete?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Yes.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Whether it is or is not, my hon. friend will not venture to say that the return as brought down stating that this dredge cost $150,000 was a correct return?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Certainly.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: I do not think on reflection that my hon. friend from Westmorland (Mr. Emmerson) would say so.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: I would say so.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: The fact of the matter is that these items, $9,300 and $7,000 were both paid in connection with this dredge, and are part of the cost of the dredge. This increase, a little over $16,000, and yet my hon. friend says that the return showing that the cost was $150,000 wTas a correct return.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext:
I know nothing about the matter. I was only giving my judg-

ment. As I understand it a return was moved for the original cost of a dredge which was purchased at Massena, New York, and a certain amount was paid for the dredge as she then existed. What they paid for the dredge there is the cost of the dredge.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: No.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: That is my view of it. Subsequently they also purchased spare parts.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext:
From the original seller?
Mr. EMMERSON They may have purchased them from the original seller or anybody else; it does not make any difference. It is not part of the cost, and need not necessarily have come with the dredge.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Suppose the hon. member for Westmorland goes out and buys a dredge, he buys duplicate parts, and the whole costs him $150,000; if I asked him how much that dredge cost him, would he leave off the duplicate parts? Would he not include them with what he had paid for the dredge?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: If the duplicate parts were a portion of the dredge they would be included in the total cost of $150,000, as the cost price, and the very fact that these parts were purchased apart from the price of $150,000 shows that they are not a part of the dredge, and are not part of the original cost of the dredge. The fact that the dredge itself was deficient with respect to the boiler, and that subsequently a new boiler was placed therein does not prove that the cost of the new boiler would have to be considered as part of the original cost of the dredge at Massena, or wherever she was purchased. That is my judgment. It is the difference between tweedle-dee and tweedle-dum. It is like purchasing a house, there are certain fixtures that go with the house, and there are certain other items that do not.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: What is the total cost of the house?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: The total cost of the house is, say $10,000. The fixtures do not go with it, and they are subsequently purchased, they are additional, and are not included in the original cost. I have in my mind an illustration in regard to myself where a certain fixed sum was paid for a house, and subseqeuntly I purchased certain other fixtures, incidental to the house, but not part of the original cost price. If parties asked me what that house had cost me, I would not include these other items.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Does this return ask for the original cost of this dredge?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Yes, the original cost.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: It says the price paid for the dredge.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: That makes it absolutely clear. Another reason is that the dredge was purchased at so much, these duplicate parts were separately invoiced, and the agreement was that they would sell them at the invoice price. Invoices were furnished showing that they were absolutely and entirely separate from the purchase of the dredge.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: If the minister purchased a dredge would he not believe that he had purchased something that was complete, and ready for work? What would he regard as a complete dredge? Must it not include the equipment so that it can go on and dredge?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Yes.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: It would not be a dredge if there were some dippers absent?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: No.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Well, then must not the equipment of the dredge be part of the dredge?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Yes.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Then I take it that these parts should go along with it.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: No, they do not go along.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: If I buy a threshing machine, I expect to get certain equipment. There are certain duplicate parts that always go along with it.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: That depends on the bargain.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: No, that is the regular custom. You know you are getting parts in duplicate, but you get a completed machine, so that you can go to work with it at any time. What amuses the hon. member for Westmorland?

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: He is wondering what is the bearing on the discussion.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: I was not laughing at my hon. friend (Mr. Sproule). He need not be sensitive. I certainly would not think of laughing at him. I had better be laughing than looking glum.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: I was saying that if I purchased a threshing machine I would get certain other parts in duplicate. It is supposed to be a completed machine. A completed dredge is a dredge with all the necessary parts to make it work.

subtopic: HALIFAX HARBOUR-BIG GUN PRACTICE AND THE FISHERMEN.
speechtext: Yes.

I think my hon. friend wras not here before recess. I stated then that the price of the dredge at first was to be $150,000. We did raise the objection, and on that ground, and as a result of further negotiations, the price was reduced to $140,000. Now the difference between that $140,000, and the amount of $157,000 mentioned in the Auditor General's Report, is made up by what the department paid for the duplicate parts, which, as I have said, were bought separately from the dredge, and were not in. the contract for the dredge, except that they had to be taken at the invoice prices. This return was not brought down until the 24th of February last. All this explanation was not made to appear in the Auditor General's Report, the last report I understand before that. Surely there was time enough to have these things brought down, and surely there is an indication at least of a very dangerous kind of carelessness, if this kind of thing can exist in a well ordered department of this government.
