Where there is no special vote.
It appears to me, when asking for such a large amount as $675,000, that the minister must have some knowledge as to where this amount will be expended.
I gave that when the hon. gentleman was not here. I gave the list of a large number of places where dredging was urgently required.
Has the minister given the places where this amount is to be expended?

I gave the names of a large number of places in Nova Scotia,
New Brunswick and Prince Edward Island where dredging was urgently required' but I stated that we could not do all the dredging at these places this year, and I also mentioned the fact that there were quite a number of other places which I had not mentioned in the three provinces where dredging was urgently required, and that we will not have enough money to do all the dredging work at these places during the coming season, but we will have to use our best judgment to pick out those places where dredging has been urgently required, and do dredging at the other places after the next session of parliament, coming for a further appropriation. But, we have not yet decided as to the different places. We have to go through, and it is a very great labour requiring a great deal of care, all the reports, we have to look into the question of the necessity of the work, the depth of the water, the size of vessels frequenting the port, and then exercise our best judgment and pick out the places where we think the work of dredging should go on. In regard to Bathurst harbour, that work will either be done by a government dredge, or public tenders will be invited when we decide to go on with it.
That is for the larger work?
Yes.
Is it intended to expend any of this money in dredging the Oromocto shoals on the St. John riven during the coming season?
It has not been positively decided, but I recognize the necessity for the work, and I think it is not unlikely that a portion of the money will be expended there.
Has the minister any requests for that work?
Yes, we have had requests from the board of trade at Fredericton and, I think, from the council.
I understand that there was a contract let for the work in the summer of 1908 to the Maritime Dredging and Construction Company. Was any work done under that contract?
Yes.
How much was paid under the contract?
That was in 1908. I have not that here, but my hon. friend can find it in the Auditor General's Report. If the work is continued there public tenders will be invited during this season for it.

That is information that I would like to have. It is a portion of the St. John river in which the people of my constituency are very much interested inasmuch as the depth of water on the shoals governs the size of vessels that are able to get up to Fredericton, and we understand that these shoals have been filling up, and that navigation has been very considerably interfered with during the last year or two. I would like to know just what work was done under the contract let in 1908, how much was paid to the contractors under it, and if any work was - done during the past year.
Of course, my hon. friend can find out from the report of 1908.
The minister surely has that.
I do not keep everything in my pocket or in my head. There must be 1,250 of 1,500 works going on in different parts of Canada, and I do not keep all the details in my head.
The minister, or his officers should have that information.
No, my officers should not either. We are asking for an appropriation for 1910-11. It does not follow that when we come here we will have information as to all the work which was done two years ago.
I think I am entitled as a member of the committee to ask the minister for it, and the minister is entitled to give it to me.

I will be very glad to get it for the hon. gentleman, and furnish it to him at a convenient time, but I will not go down to my office to-night, and unlock the office to get it. I am not going to send the chief engineer, and I am not going, unless by the desire of this committee, to stay my estimates until it can be hunted up.
It is for the minister to exercise his. own judgment.

My hon. friend wanted to know about the work at Oromocto. Last year a channel 18,400 feet long, 225 feet wide, and with a depth of 11 feet was dredged. That was quite an important portion of the work.
What was the depth?
If my hon. friend does not, by the exercise of his abundant ingenuity, keep my estimates from passing, I propose to go on with the work on the Oromocto shoals during the coming year.

I do not think that the minister seriously supposes the House Mr. PUGSLEY.
would believe that I could prevent him, by asking a few questions, from going on with a work which he says is necessary_ in the public interest. If that is the thing that influences the minister in the appropriation and expenditure of public moneys the sooner members of this House, and the people of the country know it the better. Is it possible that a little personal feeling which may animate him in reference to an lion, member would influence him in the expenditure of the public moneys of the country? I have asked the minister only for information which I am entitled to receive. All of the questions that I have asked the minister have been pertinent questions, and I propose to continue asking pertinent questions about any public work in New Brunswick or any other part of the Dominion that the people's representatives are interested in, and that we have a right to ask him about. I made a very reasonable request of the Minister of Public Works to allow this item to stand, because he mentioned a long list of places in the provinces of Nova Scotia and New Brunswick in which he said that he proposed to do dredging during the coming year; or rather, he mentioned a long list of places from which he had urgent requests for dredging. I wanted to ascertain at which of the places mentioned it has been decided that dredging shall be done during the coming year.

I can say to my hon. friend that if the matter stood for a fortnight, I could give no more information as to where the dredging will be done in the coming year than I have given to-night, because it has not yet been decided. I did not -mean that the course taken by the hon. gentleman would at all influence me so far as the dredging at Oromocto is concerned, but if the hon. gentleman is sincerely desirous of having dredging done there or anywhere else, he does not take the best means of showing his sympathy for the work by obstructing the passing of the estimates.

I leave it to members on both sides of this House if I have attempted to obstruct the estimates, 'or if the questions which I have put to the minister are not reasonable questions respecting items of expenditure to which we are all entitled to the fullest information, or if I have asked for information which hon. members of this House ought not to have before voting away such a large amount of money as this. I told the fninister some time ago that I did not propose to discuss any of those matters on which criticism might be made. I wanted to get information as to the different places in the maritime provinces where dredging is proposed to be done, and I suggested to the minister, I thought very courteously, that the item

had better stand, because there was information "which the minister has admitted that he is not in a position to give to-night; and I advance the additional reason that there were matters which I wished to discuss under the head of dredging for the maritime provinces, but which are not ripe for discussion at the present time because some of those matters are under investigation by the Public Accounts Committee. I cannot conceive of any good reason that the minister can have for dredging contracts of the Department of Public Works. Surely he does not hope, by forcing this item through at this late hour, in a very slim house, to escape the discussion of these matters.
There will be the fullest opportunity for discussion that the hon. gentleman desires.
I have been in .this House for six sessions, and this is the first time I have heard a minister refuse to allow an item to stand so that a matter may be discussed which a member desires to discuss.

If my hon. friend will permit me, the proper time to discuss matters which are under investigation by the Public Accounts Committee is when the report of the committee is presented. Then it may be fully and completely discussed; my hon. friend may take all the time he wishes. We shall have the report of the committee and the evidence, and everything can be gone into. But surely my hon. friend will not suggest that it is reasonable that important items of supply should be delayed until the Public Accounts Committee makes its report. Therefore, I must urge that we proceed with the business before the committee.

I wish to renew the suggestion I have made to the leader of the House. It is now twelve o'clock, and whatever may be said of the opposition, I am sure that to-day and on other days when the hon. Minister of Public Works has had his estimates before the committee, there has been no suggestion of obstruction. I am sure that the leader of the House will recognize that this request is a reasonable one.

speechtext: Surely my hon. friend will accept the assurances of the minister that not only will he furnish the information, but put the hon. gentleman in possession of it in advance of any discussion he may require.

In Supply?

Halton (Mr. Henderson) has been waiting here all evening for this item, and 1 would not like the committee to rise unless he desires it.

It is very kind of the Minister of Public Works to leave the matter with myself, but I would not pretend to govern the procedure of the House. I have waited here patiently during the whole evening for the purpose of referring to a particular matter with which I know the hon. minister is quite familiar. He was good enough, during the course of the evening, to refer to a considerable number of dredging appropriations throughout the province of Ontario, more particularly the larger places, such as Port Arthur, Tiifin, Midland, Goderich and down on the Lake Erie shore, and in the city of Toronto, but did not make any reference to the smaller ports. I was afraid he was going to overlook them. I very much desire that the minister shall pay some attention to the smaller harbours that require immediate attention if they are to be of use to the public. I refer particularly to Oakville. This is not new to the minister, because during the month of February I had the pleasure of drawing his attention to the great need, the urgent need, of dredging that harbour as well as of making improvements also to the wharf. The minister kindly suggested that when this item was up for discussion, I might draw attention to it, and this I now do. I do not know that the minister has ever visited Oakville. If not, I would cordially invite him to come there at the first opportunity. I think that should he visit that beautiful town and note its surroundings and its great need of harbour improvements, it would not be necessary for me, particularly at this hour of the morning, to urge upon him to make a small appropriation for those improvements. Oakville is about midway between Toronto and Hamilton, on the north shore of Lake Ontario. It is a town of considerable importance. In the past there has been considerable shipping at that port, but as nothing has been done for the last six or seven years to keep the harbour in
good shape there is no means of vessels getting in except those of very light draft. The result is that very little trade is carried on in comparison with what was done in former years. And unless the government takes action I am afraid that_ the prospect for the future is not very bright. The difficulty with the harbour is a lack of depth of water due to the fact that the dredging has been neglected. I not merely ask the minister, but I urge him, urge him as strongly as I can, to do something for this harbour. Nothing has been expended there since 1902-3-almost seven years. During that time, the harbour has been so filled up that only vessels of the lightest draft are able to go in. The result is that the trade in flour, grain, apples and small fruits that was carried on there has not been carried on through the harbour of recent years, nor can it be unless some improvement is made. Nor can the passenger boats between Toronto and Hamilton call there as they formerly did. I would remind the minister that Oakville is practically a Toronto suburb so far as residents are concerned. Many Toronto people come out to Oakville to live. They come out in the evening and return to their work in Toronto in the morning. Had we communication by water, Oakville could be made a summer resort of much greater importance than it is. The water communication would be more agreeable to many than the railway. I understand the minister has an estimate from his district engineer of the probable cost of this dredging; I have been led by the district engineer to understand that he forwarded a report or survey to the minister showing the amount that would probably be required. I do not know the contents of that report. I should be very glad if the minister would give us an idea about how much would be required to put the harbour of Oakville in proper shape.
Now, I leave the matter to the minister's own judgment. I think he will be disposed .to treat the town of Oakville fairly and do what little is necessary-I do not say too little, for I do not want him to be niggardly in the appropriation. I want him to do what is necessary to put the harbour in good shape, both with regard to depth of water and to the improvement of the wharf where necessary. I am told that some stone filling is required, and also that there are some projecting timbers that interfere with vessels coming to the dock. I am sure that if the minister undertakes .the work, he will see to it that it is properly done. I make the appeal to him to do this work, and I trust I may meet with a favourable response.

The claims of Oakville have been very strongly urged upon my attention by residents of the locality as well

as by my hon. friend (Mr. Henderson) who has very properly presented the matter, not only once but two or three times to my attention. I am impressed with the desirability of doing dredging work at Oakville so as to allow steamers to enter the harbour. At present they are obliged to lie outside of the wharf or breakwater, and, when storms arise, this is not a safe place for them to lie. If we had some such improvements as are suggested by my hon. friend, it would be greatly to the advantage of the people of Oakville. The report of the engineer has been received. I have not it here at the moment, but my recollection is that about $10,000 was estimated to make very effective improvements. In making the division of the amount we are asking for Ontario and Quebec, the claims of Oakville will receive careful consideration. While I cannot say positively that the work will be done, yet I can assure mv hon. friend that I shall be disappointed if I do not find myself able to do this work at Oakville during the coming year.
